cues.en: The Riemann zeta function.
cues.zh: 黎曼ζ函数。

cues.en: This is one of those objects in modern math that a lot of you might have heard of, but which can be really difficult to understand.
cues.zh: 这是现代数学中很多人可能听说过、但很难真正理解的一个对象。

cues.en: Don't worry. I'll explain that animation that you just saw in a few minutes.
cues.zh: 别担心。几分钟后我会解释你刚才看到的动画。

cues.en: A lot of people know about this function because there's a $1,000,000 prize out for anyone who can figure out when it equals zero,
cues.zh: 很多人知道这个函数，是因为有人悬赏 100 万美元，奖励能找出它何时等于零的人，

cues.en: an open problem known as the Riemann hypothesis.
cues.zh: 这是一道尚未解决的难题，叫作黎曼猜想。

cues.en: Some of you may have heard of it in the context of the divergent sum one plus two plus three plus four, on and on up to infinity.
cues.zh: 你们有些人可能听说过它与这个发散级数有关：一加二加三加四，一直加到无穷。

cues.en: You see, there's a sense in which the sum equals negative one twelfth, which seems nonsensical if not obviously wrong.
cues.zh: 你看，从某种意义上说，这个级数的和等于负十二分之一；这听起来毫无道理，甚至显然是错的。

cues.en: But a common way to define what this equation is actually saying uses the Riemann zeta function.
cues.zh: 不过，要解释这个等式实际表达什么，常见的一种方式会用到黎曼ζ函数。

cues.en: But as any casual math enthusiast who started to read into this knows, its definition references this one idea called analytic continuation,
cues.zh: 但任何随手查阅相关资料的数学爱好者都会发现，这个函数的定义提到了一个叫作解析延拓的概念，

cues.en: which has to do with complex valued functions.
cues.zh: 它涉及复值函数。

cues.en: And this idea can be frustratingly opaque and unintuitive.
cues.zh: 而这个概念可能晦涩得让人抓狂，也很难凭直觉理解。

cues.en: So what I'd like to do here is just show you all what this zeta function actually looks like,
cues.zh: 所以，我想在这里给大家看看这个ζ函数实际是什么样子，

cues.en: and to explain what this idea of analytic continuation is in a visual and more intuitive way.
cues.zh: 并用可视化、更直观的方式解释解析延拓这个概念。

cues.en: I'm assuming that you know about complex numbers and that you're comfortable working with them. And I'm tempted to say that you should know calculus since analytic continuation is all about derivatives,
cues.zh: 我先假设你们了解复数，也能熟练地使用它们。我本来想说，你们还应该懂微积分，因为解析延拓完全离不开导数，

cues.en: but for the way I'm planning to present things, think you might actually be fine without that.
cues.zh: 但按我打算讲解的方式，你们其实不懂微积分也没关系。

cues.en: So to jump right into it, let's just define what this zeta function is. For a given input, where we commonly use the variable s, the function is one over one to the s, which is always one, plus one over two to the s, plus one over three to the s, plus one over four to the s, on and on and on, summing up over all natural numbers.
cues.zh: 言归正传，我们先来定义一下这个 zeta 函数。对于给定的输入（通常用变量 $s$ 表示），这个函数就是 1 比上 1 的 $s$ 次方（始终是 1），加上 1 比上 2 的 $s$ 次方，加上 1 比上 3 的 $s$ 次方，加上 1 比上 4 的 $s$ 次方，以此类推，对所有自然数求和。

cues.en: So for example, let's say you plug in a value like s equals two.
cues.zh: 举个例子，假设你代入一个值，比如 $s$ 等于 2。

cues.en: You'd get one plus one over four plus one over nine plus one sixteenth.
cues.zh: 你会得到 1 加上 4 分之 1 加上 9 分之 1 加上 16 分之 1。

cues.en: And as you keep adding more and more reciprocals of squares, this just so happens to approach pi squared over six, which is around 1.645.
cues.zh: 随着你不断累加越来越多的平方倒数，它刚好会趋近于 $\pi$ 方除以 6，大约是 1.645。

cues.en: There's a very beautiful reason for why pi shows up here, and I might do a video on it at a later date, but that's just the tip of the iceberg for why this function is beautiful.
cues.zh: $\pi$ 为什么会出现在这里，背后有一个非常美妙的原因，我以后可能会专门出一期视频来讲，但这只是这个函数美妙之处的冰山一角。

cues.en: You could do the same thing for other inputs s, like three or four, and sometimes you get other interesting values.
cues.zh: 你可以对其他 $s$ 的输入做同样的事情，比如 3 或 4，有时你会得到其他有趣的值。

cues.en: And so far, everything feels pretty reasonable. You're adding up smaller and smaller amounts, and these sums approach some number.
cues.zh: 到目前为止，这一切看起来都挺合理的。你把越来越小的数值加起来，这些和会趋近于某个数字。

cues.en: Great. No craziness here.
cues.zh: 很好，一点也不疯狂。

cues.en: Yet, if you were to read about it, you might see some people say that zeta of negative one equals
cues.zh: 然而，如果你去阅读相关资料，可能会看到有人说 zeta(-1) 等于

cues.en: negative one twelfth.
cues.zh: 负十二分之一。

cues.en: But looking at this infinite sum, that doesn't make any sense. When you raise each term to the negative one, flipping each fraction,
cues.zh: 但看看这个无穷级数，这根本说不通。当你把每一项都提到负一次方，把每个分数颠倒过来，

cues.en: you get one plus two plus three plus four on and on over all natural numbers. And obviously, that doesn't approach anything, certainly not negative one twelfth. Right?
cues.zh: 你会得到 1 加 2 加 3 加 4，一直到所有的自然数。很显然，这根本不会趋近于任何数，更不可能是负十二分之一。对吧？

cues.en: And as any mercenary looking into the Riemann hypothesis knows, this function is said to have trivial zeros at negative even numbers.
cues.zh: 正如任何研究黎曼猜想的雇佣兵所知，这个函数据说在负偶数处有平凡零点。

cues.en: So for example, that would mean that zeta of negative two equals zero.
cues.zh: 比如，这意味着zeta(-2)等于零。

cues.en: But when you plug in negative two, it gives you one plus four plus nine plus 16 on and on, which again obviously doesn't approach anything, much less zero. Right?
cues.zh: 但当你代入-2时，得到的是1+4+9+16一直加下去，这显然又不趋近于任何值，更不用说零了，对吧？

cues.en: Well, we'll get to negative values in a few minutes, but for right now, let's just say the only thing that seems reasonable.
cues.zh: 我们几分钟后会讨论负值，但现在，我们只能说唯一看起来合理的做法是——

cues.en: This function only makes sense when s is greater than one, which is when this sum converges.
cues.zh: 这个函数只在s大于1时才有意义，也就是这个和收敛的时候。

cues.en: So far, it's simply not defined for other values.
cues.zh: 到目前为止，它在其他值上根本没有定义。

cues.en: Now with that said, Bernard Riemann was somewhat of a father to complex analysis,
cues.zh: 话虽如此，Bernhard Riemann可以说是复分析之父，

cues.en: which is the study of functions that have complex numbers as inputs and outputs.
cues.zh: 复分析研究的是输入和输出都是复数的函数。

cues.en: So rather than just thinking about how this sum takes a number s on the real number line to another number on the real number line,
cues.zh: 所以他不只是考虑这个和如何把实数轴上的数s映射到实数轴上的另一个数，

cues.en: his main focus was on understanding what happens when you plug in a complex value for s.
cues.zh: 他的主要关注点是理解当你代入一个复数值作为s时会发生什么。

cues.en: So for example, maybe instead of plugging in two,
cues.zh: 比如，也许你不代入2，

cues.en: you would plug in two plus I.
cues.zh: 而是代入2+i。

cues.en: Now if you've never seen the idea of raising a number to the power of a complex value, it can feel kind of strange at first because it no longer has anything to do with repeated multiplication.
cues.zh: 如果你从没见过把一个数提升到复数次幂的概念，一开始可能会觉得很奇怪，因为它不再和重复乘法有任何关系了。

cues.en: But mathematicians found that there is a very nice and very natural way to extend the definition of exponents
cues.zh: 但数学家们发现，有一种非常优美且自然的方式可以把指数的定义

cues.en: beyond their familiar territory of real numbers and into the realm of complex values.
cues.zh: 从熟悉的实数领域扩展到复数领域。

cues.en: It's not super crucial to understand complex exponents for where I'm going with this video, but I think it'll still be nice if we just summarize the gist of it here.
cues.zh: 对于这段视频接下来要讲的内容，理解复数指数不是特别重要，不过我觉得还是可以先简单总结一下它的要点。

cues.en: The basic idea is that when you write something like one half to the power of a complex number, you split it up as one half to the real part times one half to the pure imaginary part.
cues.zh: 基本思路是：像“二分之一的复数次方”这样的式子，可以拆成“二分之一的实部次方”，再乘以“二分之一的纯虚部次方”。

cues.en: We're good on one half to the real part. There's no issues there. But what about raising something to a pure imaginary number?
cues.zh: 二分之一的实数次方我们已经很熟悉了，没什么问题。但把一个数提升到纯虚数次方会怎样呢？

cues.en: Well, the result is gonna be some complex number on the unit circle in the complex plane.
cues.zh: 结果会是复平面单位圆上的某个复数。

cues.en: As you let that pure imaginary input walk up and down the imaginary line,
cues.zh: 当你让这个纯虚数输入沿着虚轴上下移动时，

cues.en: the resulting output walks around that unit circle.
cues.zh: 对应的输出也会沿着单位圆转动。

cues.en: For a base like one half, the output walks around the unit circle somewhat slowly.
cues.zh: 如果底数是二分之一，输出沿单位圆转动得比较慢。

cues.en: But for a base that's farther away from one, like one ninth,
cues.zh: 但如果底数离 1 更远，比如九分之一，

cues.en: then as you let this input walk up and down the imaginary axis, the corresponding output is gonna walk around the unit circle more quickly.
cues.zh: 那么当输入沿着虚轴上下移动时，对应的输出就会沿单位圆转得更快。

cues.en: If you've never seen this and you're wondering why on earth this happens, I've left a few links to good resources in the description.
cues.zh: 如果你以前没见过这个，想知道这到底是为什么，我在视频简介里放了几个不错的参考链接。

cues.en: For here, I'm just gonna move forward with the what without the why.
cues.zh: 这里我就先讲是什么，暂时不解释为什么。

cues.en: The main takeaway is that when you raise something like one half to the power of two plus I, which is one half squared times one half to the I,
cues.zh: 重点是，像二分之一的 2+i 次方这样的式子，可以写成二分之一的平方，乘以二分之一的 i 次方。

cues.en: that one half to the I part is gonna be on the unit circle, meaning it has an absolute value of one.
cues.zh: 二分之一的 i 次方会落在单位圆上，也就是说，它的绝对值是 1。

cues.en: So when you multiply it, it doesn't change the size of the number. It just takes that one fourth and rotates it somewhat.
cues.zh: 所以当你乘以它时，数字的大小并没有改变。它只是把那四分之一旋转了一定角度。

cues.en: So if you were to plug in two plus I to the zeta function,
cues.zh: 所以如果你把 $2+i$ 代入 zeta 函数，

cues.en: one way to think about what it does is to start off with all of the terms raised to the power of two, which you can think of as piecing together lines whose lengths are the reciprocals of squares of numbers,
cues.zh: 理解它的一种方式是，从所有项都提升到 2 次方开始，你可以把它想象成把长度为数字平方倒数的线段拼凑起来，

cues.en: which, like I said before, converges to pi squared over six.
cues.zh: 就像我之前说的，它收敛于 $\pi^2/6$。

cues.en: Then when you change that input from two up to two plus I,
cues.zh: 然后，当你把输入从 2 改为 $2+i$ 时，

cues.en: each of these lines gets rotated by some amount.
cues.zh: 其中的每一条线段都会旋转一定的角度。

cues.en: But importantly, the lengths of those lines won't change, so the sum still converges.
cues.zh: 但重要的是，这些线段的长度不会改变，所以总和仍然是收敛的。

cues.en: It just does so in a spiral to some specific point on the complex plane.
cues.zh: 它只是以螺旋形收敛到复平面上的某个特定点。

cues.en: Here, let me show what it looks like when I vary the input s, represented with this yellow dot on the complex plane, where this spiral sum is always gonna be showing the converging value for zeta of s.
cues.zh: 来，我展示一下当我改变输入 $s$（用复平面上的这个黄色圆点表示）时的样子，这个螺旋形的和将始终显示 zeta(s) 的收敛值。

cues.en: What this means is that zeta of s, defined as this infinite sum, is a perfectly reasonable complex function as long as the real part of the input is greater than one, meaning the input s sits somewhere on this right half of the complex plane.
cues.zh: 这意味着，定义为这个无穷级数的 zeta(s)，只要输入的实部大于 1，就是一个完全合理的复变函数，也就是说输入 $s$ 位于复平面的右半部分。

cues.en: Again, this is because it's the real part of s that determines the size of each number, while the imaginary part just dictates some rotation.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这是因为正是 $s$ 的实部决定了每个数字的大小，而虚部只决定了旋转。

cues.en: So now what I want to do is visualize this function.
cues.zh: 所以现在我想做的是把这个函数可视化。

cues.en: It takes in inputs on the right half of the complex plane and spits out outputs somewhere else in the complex plane.
cues.zh: 它接收复平面右半部分的输入，然后在复平面的某个其他地方吐出输出。

cues.en: A super nice way to understand complex functions is to visualize them as transformations,
cues.zh: 理解复变函数的一个超级好方法是将它们可视化为变换，

cues.en: meaning you look at every possible input to the function and just let it move over to the corresponding output.
cues.zh: 意思是你观察函数的每一个可能输入，然后让它移动到对应的输出位置。

cues.en: For example, let's take a moment and try to visualize something a little bit easier than the zeta function. Say f of s is equal to s squared.
cues.zh: 例如，我们花点时间试着想象一个比 zeta 函数稍稍简单一点的东西。比如 $f(s)$ 等于 $s$ 的平方。

cues.en: When you plug in s equals two, you get four. So we'll end up moving that point at two over to the point at four.
cues.zh: 当你代入 $s$ 等于 2 时，结果是 4。所以我们最终会把位于 2 的那个点移动到位于 4 的点上。

cues.en: When you plug in negative one, you get one.
cues.zh: 当你代入负一时，结果是一。

cues.en: So the point over here at negative one is gonna end up moving over to the point at one.
cues.zh: 所以这边负一处的点最终会移动到一处的点。

cues.en: When you plug in I, by definition, its square is negative one, so it's gonna move over here to negative one.
cues.zh: 当你代入 $i$ 时，根据定义，它的平方是负一，所以它会移动到这里的负一。

cues.en: Now I'm gonna add on a more colorful grid, and this is just because things are about to start moving, and it's kinda nice to have something to distinguish grid lines during that movement. From here, I'll tell the computer to move every single point on this grid over to its corresponding output under the function f of s equals s squared. Here's what it looks like.
cues.zh: 现在我要加上一个色彩更丰富的网格，这只是因为接下来事物要开始运动了，而且在运动过程中能有些东西来区分网格线会很不错。接下来，我会让计算机把这个网格上的每一个点都移动到它在 $f(s) = s^2$ 这个函数下的对应输出位置。这就是它的样子。

cues.en: That can be a lot to take in, so I'll go ahead and play it again. And this time, focus on one of the marked points, and notice how it moves over to the point corresponding to its square.
cues.zh: 信息量可能有点大，所以我再放一遍。这一次，关注其中一个标记的点，注意它是如何移动到与其平方相对应的点的。

cues.en: It can be a little complicated to see all of the points moving all at once, but the reward is that this gives us a very rich picture for what the complex function is actually doing, and it all happens in just two dimensions.
cues.zh: 要一眼看出所有点同时运动可能会有点复杂，但回报是，这让我们对这个复变函数实际在做什么有了非常丰富的直观理解，而且这一切都发生在仅仅二维的空间里。

cues.en: So back to the zeta function, we have this infinite sum, which is a function of some complex number s, and we feel good and happy about plugging in values of s whose real part is greater than one and getting some meaningful output via the converging spiral sum.
cues.zh: 所以回到 zeta 函数，我们有这样一个无穷级数，它是某个复数 s 的函数。当我们代入实部大于 1 的 s 值时，会感到很舒心，并且通过收敛的螺旋级数得到一些有意义的输出。

cues.en: So to visualize this function, I'm gonna take the portion of the grid sitting on the right side of the complex plane here where the real part of numbers is greater than one, And I'm gonna tell the computer to move each point of this grid to the appropriate output.
cues.zh: 因此，为了可视化这个函数，我将选取复平面右侧这部分网格（即数字实部大于 1 的区域），然后让计算机把这个网格的每个点移动到对应的输出位置。

cues.en: It actually helps if I add a few more grid lines around the number one since that region gets stretched out by quite a bit.
cues.zh: 实际上，如果我在数字 1 周围再添加一些网格线，会很有帮助，因为那一块区域会被拉伸得比较厉害。

cues.en: Alright. So first of all, let's all just appreciate how beautiful that is. I mean, damn, that doesn't make you wanna learn more about complex functions. You have no heart.
cues.zh: 好啦。首先，让我们一起欣赏一下它是多么的美丽。我是说，天哪，如果这都没让你产生去了解更多复变函数的冲动，那你可太冷血了。

cues.en: But also, this transformed grid is just begging to be extended a little bit.
cues.zh: 而且，这个变换后的网格简直在呼唤着我们把它稍微延伸一下。

cues.en: For example, let's highlight these lines here, which represent all of the complex numbers with imaginary part I or negative I.
cues.zh: 例如，我们高亮显示这里的这些线，它们代表了所有虚部为 i 或负 i 的复数。

cues.en: After the transformation,
cues.zh: 变换之后，

cues.en: these lines make such lovely arcs before they just abruptly stop.
cues.zh: 这些线条在戛然而止之前，勾勒出了如此优美的弧线。

cues.en: Don't you wanna just, you know, continue those arcs?
cues.zh: 难道你不想，你知道的，把那些弧线延续下去吗？

cues.en: In fact, you can imagine how some altered version of the function with a definition that extends into this left half of the plane might be able to complete this picture with something that's quite pretty.
cues.zh: 事实上，你可以想象一下，如果这个函数的定义能够延伸到平面左半部分，某种修改后的版本或许能用某种非常优美的方式补全这幅画面。

cues.en: Well, this is exactly what mathematicians working with complex functions do.
cues.zh: 嗯，这正是研究复变函数的数学家们所做的事情。

cues.en: They continue the function beyond the original domain where it was defined.
cues.zh: 他们将函数延续到了最初定义它的原始域之外。

cues.en: Now as soon as we branch over into inputs where the real part is less than one, this infinite sum that we originally used to define the function doesn't make sense anymore. You'll get nonsense like adding one plus two plus three plus four on and on up to infinity.
cues.zh: 现在，一旦我们涉足实部小于 1 的输入，我们最初用来定义函数的这个无穷级数就彻底失效了。你会得到诸如 1 加 2 加 3 加 4 一直加到无穷大这样的荒谬结果。

cues.en: But just looking at this transformed version of the right half of the plane where the sum does make sense,
cues.zh: 但只要看看这个平面右半部分的变换版本——级数在那里确实是有意义的，

cues.en: it's just begging us to extend the set of points that we're considering as inputs.
cues.zh: 它就在央求我们去扩充作为输入的点的集合。

cues.en: Even if that means defining the extended function in some way that doesn't necessarily use that sum.
cues.zh: 即便这意味着用某种不一定非要用到那个级数的方式来定义扩展后的函数。

cues.en: Of course, that leaves us with the question, how would you define that function on the rest of the plane?
cues.zh: 当然，这给我们留下的问题是，你该如何在平面的其余部分定义这个函数呢？

cues.en: You might think that you could extend it any number of ways.
cues.zh: 你可能会觉得可以用无数种方式来扩展它。

cues.en: Maybe you define an extension that makes it so the point at, say, s equals negative one moves over to negative one twelfth.
cues.zh: 也许你定义了一种扩展，让比如说 $s$ 等于负一的点移动到负十二分之一。

cues.en: But maybe you squiggle on some extension that makes it land on any other value.
cues.zh: 但也许你随手画一条扩展线，让它落在任何其他值上。

cues.en: I mean, as soon as you open yourself up to the idea of defining the function differently
cues.zh: 我是说，一旦你接受用不同方式定义函数这个想法，

cues.en: for values outside that domain of convergence,
cues.zh: 针对收敛域之外的值，

cues.en: that is not based on this infinite sum,
cues.zh: 不基于这个无穷级数来定义，

cues.en: the world is your oyster, and you can have any number of extensions.
cues.zh: 那就海阔天空了，你可以有任意多种扩展方式。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: not exactly.
cues.zh: 也不完全是。

cues.en: I mean, yes, you can give any child a marker and have them extend these lines any which way, But if you add on the restriction that this new extended function has to have a derivative everywhere,
cues.zh: 我是说，没错，你可以给任何孩子一支马克笔，让他们随便怎么延长这些线，但如果你加上一个限制：这个新的扩展函数必须在处处都有导数，

cues.en: it locks us into one and only one possible extension.
cues.zh: 那就把我们锁定在了唯一一种可能的扩展上。

cues.en: I know, I know, I said that you wouldn't need to know about derivatives for this video. And even if you do know calculus, maybe you have yet to learn how to interpret derivatives for complex functions.
cues.zh: 我知道，我知道，我说过这个视频不需要懂导数。而且就算你懂微积分，也许你还没学过怎么理解复函数的导数。

cues.en: But luckily for us, there is a very nice geometric intuition that you can keep in mind for when I say a phrase like has a derivative everywhere.
cues.zh: 但幸运的是，有一个非常直观的几何直觉，你可以记住它，以便理解我说的“处处有导数”是什么意思。

cues.en: Here, to show you what I mean, let's look back at that f of s equals s squared example.
cues.zh: 这里，为了说明我的意思，让我们回顾一下 f(s) = s² 这个例子。

cues.en: Again, we think of this function as a transformation,
cues.zh: 同样，我们把这个函数看作一个变换，

cues.en: moving every point s of the complex plane over to the point s squared.
cues.zh: 把复平面上的每个点 s 移动到点 s²。

cues.en: For those of you who know calculus, you know that you can take the derivative of this function at any given input.
cues.zh: 懂微积分的同学知道，你可以对这个函数在任意给定输入处求导。

cues.en: But there's an interesting property of that transformation
cues.zh: 但这个变换有一个有趣的性质，

cues.en: that turns out to be related and almost equivalent to that fact.
cues.zh: 它恰好与这个事实相关，而且几乎是等价的。

cues.en: If you look at any two lines in the input space that intersect at some angle and consider what they turn into after the transformation,
cues.zh: 如果你看输入空间中以某个夹角相交的任意两条直线，并思考它们在经过变换后变成了什么样子，

cues.en: they will still intersect each other at that same angle.
cues.zh: 它们仍会以相同的角度彼此相交。

cues.en: The lines might get curved, and that's okay, but the important part is that the angle at which they intersect remains unchanged.
cues.zh: 线条可能会变弯曲，这没关系，但重要的是它们相交的角度保持不变。

cues.en: And this is true for any pair of lines that you choose.
cues.zh: 你所选择的任意一对直线也是如此。

cues.en: So when I say a function has a derivative everywhere,
cues.zh: 所以当我转述一个函数处处可导时，

cues.en: I want you to think about this angle preserving property that anytime two lines intersect,
cues.zh: 我想请大家思考这个保持角度的性质：每当两条线相交时，

cues.en: the angle between them remains unchanged
cues.zh: 它们之间的夹角保持不变

cues.en: after the transformation.
cues.zh: 转换之后。

cues.en: At a glance, this is easiest to appreciate by noticing how all of the curves that the grid lines turn into still intersect each other at right angles.
cues.zh: 初看起来，最容易理解这一点的方式是，注意到网格线变换后的所有曲线仍然以直角相交。

cues.en: Complex functions that have a derivative everywhere are called analytic,
cues.zh: 处处都有导数的复函数称为解析函数，

cues.en: so you can think of this term analytic as meaning angle preserving.
cues.zh: 所以你可以把这个术语“解析”理解为保角的意思。

cues.en: Admittedly, I'm lying to you a little here, but only a little bit. A slight caveat for those of you who want the full details is that at inputs where the derivative of a function is zero, instead of angles being preserved, they get multiplied by some integer.
cues.zh: 坦白说，我这里对大家稍稍撒了点谎，但真的就一点点。给想了解全部细节的人提个醒：在函数导数为零的输入点上，角度不仅不会保持不变，反而会被乘以某个整数。

cues.en: But those points are by far the minority,
cues.zh: 但这些点只占少数，

cues.en: and for almost all inputs to an analytic function, angles are preserved.
cues.zh: 对于解析函数的几乎所有输入，角度都保持不变。

cues.en: So if when I say analytic, you think angle preserving, I think that's a fine intuition to have.
cues.zh: 所以如果我说解析时，你想到的是保角，我觉得这是一种很好的直觉。

cues.en: Now if you think about it for a moment, and this is a point that I really want you to appreciate,
cues.zh: 如果你花一分钟想想看——这是我特别希望你能体会的一点，

cues.en: this is a very restrictive property.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常严格的性质。

cues.en: The angle between any pair of intersecting lines has to remain unchanged.
cues.zh: 任意一对相交直线之间的夹角必须保持不变。

cues.en: And yet, pretty much any function out there that has a name turns out to be analytic.
cues.zh: 然而，几乎所有叫得出名字的函数，最终都被证明是解析的。

cues.en: The field of complex analysis, which Riemann helped to establish in its modern form, is almost entirely about leveraging the properties of analytic functions
cues.zh: 黎曼协助建立了其现代形态的复变函数论，几乎完全是在利用解析函数的性质，

cues.en: to understand results and patterns in other fields of math and science.
cues.zh: 来理解其他数学和科学领域的成果与规律。

cues.en: The zeta function, defined by this infinite sum on the right half of the plane, is an analytic function.
cues.zh: 由平面右半部分的这个无穷级数所定义的 zeta 函数，就是一个解析函数。

cues.en: Notice how all of these curves that the grid lines turn into still intersect each other at right angles.
cues.zh: 注意看，网格线变成的所有这些曲线依然以直角相交。

cues.en: So the surprising fact about complex functions is that if you want to extend an analytic function beyond the domain where it was originally defined,
cues.zh: 所以，关于复变函数的一个惊人事实是，如果你想把一个解析函数扩展到它最初定义的域之外，

cues.en: for example, extending this zeta function into the left half of the plane,
cues.zh: 例如，将这个 zeta 函数扩展到平面的左半部分，

cues.en: then if you require that the new extended function still be analytic,
cues.zh: 那么，如果你要求这个新的扩展函数依然是解析的，

cues.en: that is that it still preserves angles everywhere,
cues.zh: 也就是它在各处仍然保持角度不变，

cues.en: it forces you into only one possible extension,
cues.zh: 这就会迫使你只有一种可能的扩展方式，

cues.en: if one exists at all.
cues.zh: 假如这种扩展确实存在的话。

cues.en: It's kind of like an infinite continuous jigsaw puzzle where this requirement of preserving angles
cues.zh: 这有点像一个无限的连续拼图，这种保持角度的要求，

cues.en: locks you into one and only one choice for how to extend it.
cues.zh: 把你的扩展选择锁死了，唯一的选择就是它。

cues.en: This process of extending an analytic function in the only way possible that's still analytic is called, as you may have guessed, analytic continuation.
cues.zh: 这种以唯一可能保持解析的方式扩展解析函数的过程，正如你所猜到的，被称为解析延拓。

cues.en: So that's how the full Riemann zeta function is defined.
cues.zh: 这就是完整黎曼zeta函数的定义方式。

cues.en: For values of s on the right half of the plane, where the real part is greater than one, just plug them into this sum and see where it converges.
cues.zh: 对于右半平面上实部大于1的 $s$ 值，直接代入这个求和式，看看它在哪里收敛。

cues.en: And that convergence might look like some kind of spiral since raising each of these terms to a complex power has the effect of rotating each one.
cues.zh: 这种收敛看起来可能有点像某种螺旋，因为将其中每一项都提升到复数幂次，会产生旋转每一项的效果。

cues.en: Then for the rest of the plane, we know that there exists one and only one way to extend this definition so that the function will still be analytic. That is, so that it still preserves angles at every single point.
cues.zh: 然后对于平面的其余部分，我们知道存在且仅有一种方法来扩展这个定义，从而使该函数仍然是解析的。也就是，它在每一个点上仍然保持角度不变。

cues.en: So we just say that by definition, the zeta function on the left half of the plane is whatever that extension happens to be.
cues.zh: 所以我们只需根据定义说明，左半平面上的zeta函数就是那个碰巧存在的扩展。

cues.en: And that's a valid definition because there's only one possible analytic continuation.
cues.zh: 这是一个有效的定义，因为只有一种可能的解析延拓。

cues.en: Notice, that's a very implicit definition.
cues.zh: 注意，这是一个非常隐式的定义。

cues.en: It just says, use the solution of this jigsaw puzzle, which through more abstract derivation we know must exist,
cues.zh: 它只是说，利用这个拼图的解——通过更抽象的推导我们知道它必然存在——

cues.en: but it doesn't specify exactly how to solve it.
cues.zh: 但它并没有明确指出如何去求解。

cues.en: Mathematicians have a pretty good grasp on what this extension looks like, but some important parts of it remain a mystery. A million dollar mystery, in fact. Let's actually take a moment and talk about the Riemann hypothesis,
cues.zh: 数学家对这个扩展的长相有了相当不错的理解，但其中一些重要部分仍然是个谜。事实上，这是一个价值百万美元的谜题。我们花点时间来聊聊黎曼猜想吧，

cues.en: the million dollar problem.
cues.zh: 那个价值百万美元的问题。

cues.en: The places where this function equals zero turn out to be quite important.
cues.zh: 这个函数等于零的地方结果非常重要。

cues.en: That is, which points get mapped onto the origin after the transformation.
cues.zh: 也就是说，在经过 Transformer 变换后，哪些点会被映射到原点。

cues.en: One thing we know about this extension is that the negative even numbers get mapped to zero.
cues.zh: 关于这个延拓，我们知道的一点是，负偶数会被映射到零。

cues.en: These are commonly called the trivial zeros.
cues.zh: 这些通常被称为平凡零点。

cues.en: The naming here stems from a long standing tradition of mathematicians
cues.zh: 这里的命名源于数学界的一个悠久传统：

cues.en: to call things trivial when they understand it quite well, even when it's a fact that is not at all obvious from the outset.
cues.zh: 当数学家对某些事物理解得相当透彻时，就会称它们为“平凡的”，尽管这个事实一开始一点也不显。

cues.en: We also know that the rest of the points that get mapped to zero sit somewhere in this vertical strip called the critical strip,
cues.zh: 我们还知道，其余被映射到零的点都位于这个被称为临界带的垂直条带中，

cues.en: and the specific placement of those nontrivial zeros
cues.zh: 而这些非平凡零点的具体位置，

cues.en: encodes a surprising information about prime numbers.
cues.zh: 蕴含着关于素数的惊人信息。

cues.en: It's actually pretty interesting why this function carries so much information about primes, and I definitely think I'll make a video about that later on, but right now things are long enough, so I'll leave it unexplained.
cues.zh: 为什么这个函数能包含这么多关于素数的信息其实非常有趣，我以后肯定会为此做一个视频，但现在内容已经够长了，所以我就先不解释了。

cues.en: Riemann hypothesized that all of these nontrivial zeros sit right in the middle of the strip on the line of numbers s whose real part is one half.
cues.zh: 黎曼假设：所有这些非平凡零点都正好位于这个条带的正中央，即实部为二分之一的数轴 $s$ 上。

cues.en: This is called the critical line.
cues.zh: 这被称为临界线。

cues.en: If that's true, it gives us a remarkably tight grasp on the pattern of prime numbers as well as many other patterns in math that stem from this.
cues.zh: 如果这是真的，它将让我们对素数的规律以及数学中由此产生的许多其他规律有极其精准的把握。

cues.en: Now so far, when I've shown what the zeta function looks like, I've only shown what it does to the portion of the grid on the screen,
cues.zh: 到目前为止，当我展示 zeta 函数的样貌时，我只展示了它对屏幕上网格部分的作用，

cues.en: and that kind of undersells its complexity.
cues.zh: 这某种程度上低估了它的复杂性。

cues.en: So if I were to highlight this critical line and apply the transformation,
cues.zh: 如果我高亮这关键的一行并应用这个变换，

cues.en: it might not seem to cross the origin at all.
cues.zh: 它看起来可能根本没有穿过原点。

cues.en: However, here's what the transformed version of more and more of that line looks like.
cues.zh: 然而，这条线越来越多的部分经过变换后是这样的。

cues.en: Notice how it's passing through the number zero many, many times.
cues.zh: 注意它是如何多次穿过数字零的。

cues.en: If you can prove that all of the nontrivial zeros sit somewhere on this line, the Clay Math Institute gives you $1,000,000.
cues.zh: 如果你能证明所有这些非平凡零点都位于这条线上，克雷数学研究所就会给你 100 万美元。

cues.en: And you'd also be proving hundreds, if not thousands, of modern math results that have already been shown contingent on this hypothesis being true.
cues.zh: 而且你还将证明成百上千个现代数学成果，这些成果已经被证明依赖于这个假设成立。

cues.en: Another thing we know about this extended function is that it maps the point negative one over to negative one twelfth.
cues.zh: 关于这个拓展函数的另一件事是，它将负一映射到负十二分之一。

cues.en: And if you plug this into the original sum, it looks like we're saying one plus two plus three plus four on and on up to infinity equals negative one twelfth.
cues.zh: 如果你把这个代入最初的和，看起来就像是在说 1 加 2 加 3 加 4 这样一直到无穷大等于负十二分之一。

cues.en: Now it might seem disingenuous to still call this a sum since the definition of the zeta function on the left half of the plane is not defined directly from this sum.
cues.zh: 现在，仍然把这叫做和可能显得有点不诚实，因为平面左半部分的 zeta 函数定义并不是直接从这个和定义的。

cues.en: Instead, it comes from analytically continuing the sum beyond the domain where it converges.
cues.zh: 相反，它来自于对收敛域之外的和进行解析延拓。

cues.en: That is solving the jigsaw puzzle that began on the right half of the plane.
cues.zh: 也就是解决那个在平面右半部分开始的拼图游戏。

cues.en: That said, you have to admit that the uniqueness of this analytic continuation,
cues.zh: 话虽如此，你不得不承认这种解析延拓的唯一性，

cues.en: the fact that the jigsaw puzzle has only one solution,
cues.zh: 也就是这个拼图游戏只有一个解的事实，

cues.en: is very suggestive of some intrinsic connection between these extended values and the original sum.
cues.zh: 非常暗示了这些扩展值与最初的和之间存在某种内在的联系。
